before.objective:
Find a model that maximizes forecasting accuracy on the full expanded 1,264-series panel. Accuracy is the primary objective. Speed is secondary: optimize runtime without sacrificing forecasting performance. Additional complexity or compute is acceptable when it improves accuracy.

Start from the better new asset configuration. Test the prior best at asset level; promote each stronger model. Run both asset-level TestFolio-style configurations, with and without replacement. Use whichever scores worse on identical coverage as the sole baseline; preserve prior results and remove FAST. Official scores and recomputed baselines use 1,000 sims; screens may use fewer.

Keep the search open. Ideas may come from this panel’s results, weaknesses in existing models, earlier panels, academic papers, credible internet sources, diagnostics, or other promising reasoning. Earlier panels are optional supporting evidence. Prefer simple, intuitive solutions, while considering more complex approaches when warranted.

Use historical outperformance on earlier panels as a reference for the ambition of the search. Reaching that reference does not justify stopping early, and failing to reach it does not require continuing once the evidence-based stopping condition is met.

During development, use thorough representative tests across major asset classes, model families, forecast horizons and relevant subgroups. Evaluate promising improvements broadly before drawing conclusions. Keep the expanded panel data and single main scoring protocol fixed. Forecast at asset level: simulate constituent asset paths jointly, then apply portfolio weights and rebalancing within each path. This is mandatory for the baseline and every future candidate, including the current best model. Portfolios collectively contribute up to 50% of the overall score. Diagnostics do not affect the score or model selection. Official scores: only both configurations and current best; compare to the worse on identical coverage. Share 12 available workers across concurrent candidates. Forecast fitting must use only history available at each forecast date, without look-ahead or dependence on previous out-of-sample scores. Compare models on identical coverage and disclose failures and regressions.

Actively seek further improvements after finding a winner. Do not stop merely because a model beats Public, a few variants fail, or a small improvement has been achieved. Continue until the accumulated research and testing support your judgment that performance has been maximized on this panel and no further credible improvements remain worth testing. Speculative means pursuing changes that existing evidence suggests are unlikely to improve performance, without new evidence or a materially different mechanism that justifies reconsidering them. An untested idea is not automatically speculative. Once no credible, non-speculative improvements remain worth testing, stop rather than exhaust every imaginable variation. Explain the evidence supporting that stopping judgment.

Once that stopping point is reached, automatically launch the complete panel suite in the background with both configurations and the final best model at 1,000 simulations per forecast. Let it finish without waiting for another launch approval. Preserve reproducible evidence and report the complete matched results, the single main score, failures and runtime.

Maintain a catalogue and running count of every unique model tested on the full panel, including models that do not improve performance. Record each model’s definition and version, the single main score, coverage, failures, runtime and reproducibility details. Count identical reruns once. Preserve implementations, scoring documentation and complete results in the research repository, using repository-linked archives for large files. Keep these records after removing a model from active testing. Verify remote preservation and recovery before removing completed local outputs.
